one_month_reasoning: Events in the window. (1) Q3 results before the open on Oct 29 (confirmed) [9]. Consensus is about $9.8-9.9 EPS on $22.1-22.4B, below Q2's $23.0B because of guided seasonality [1, 9]. Lilly beat Q2 by about $1.8-2.3 despite $3.03 of IPR&D [1], Medicare Bridge starts are at 700k with 70% on Lilly [22], and Foundayo was about 47.5k weekly scripts and rising [6], so the bar looks beatable. The risks are a further step-down in US net price (underlying -9% in Q2 [1]) and cautious 2027 commentary on employer coverage (about 1 in 10 large employers that cover obesity GLP-1s expect to drop it in 2027 [38, 39]). (2) CVS Caremark restores Zepbound as co-preferred on Oct 1 [25, 26]; it adds volume but no IQVIA read on it will exist before Q3. (3) EASD ended Oct 2 with ACHIEVE-4 and TRIUMPH-2 positive [20, 21]; already in the price. (4) The 7th Circuit retatrutide opinion could come at any time after the Sep 24 argument [43], but opinions usually take weeks to months, so I give it a small chance of landing in the window. Changed from round 1: Novo's CagriSema decision most likely lands around mid-December (filed 2025-12-18, no PDUFA disclosed), so it is out of the window; and September was flat ($1,156.73 to $1,157.08 [45]), so there is no oversold rebound to bank on. I tilt the median slightly up to about $1,155 (+0.4%) for the beat-and-raise pattern, with a 10.5% monthly sigma mixed 85/15 with 15% for the earnings gap. P(>= spot) is 0.516.

fair_value.method: A blend of two P/E methods. NTM EPS at the horizon of about $52.0 (0.25 x CY27 $47.5 + 0.75 x CY28 $53.5) x 22.5x = $1,170 (weight 0.6), and CY2027 consensus EPS of $47.5 x 25.0x = $1,188 (weight 0.4). The blend is about $1,177, rounded to $1,175.

I sit about $1 above the top of that range because 2027 consensus has been revised up ($44.49 to $47.5 in 90 days) and the 2028 aggregates lag it, and because Guggenheim's Foundayo upgrade ($3.7B in 2028 [6]) and CVS co-preferred access [25] are recent. I no longer use $56.5 (2027 x 1.19): the 2028 revenue consensus is only about +11.6%, roughly 14% of large employers have dropped or plan to drop obesity GLP-1 coverage by 2027 [38, 39], and the Medicare Bridge ends 2027-12-31 with no successor [42], which weighs on 2028 volume

Spot $1,149.85 / $47.5 = 24.2x forward today. I take about 1.7 turns off as EPS growth slows from about 20% (2027) to about 12-13% (2028). Unchanged from round 1: the lower growth and the Medicare-cliff overhang [42] argue for less, while the ACHIEVE-4 safety data [20] and a retatrutide BLA in Q1 2027 argue for more; the 7th Circuit classification ruling [43] is a two-way risk to the terminal multiple

bear.story: Net price erosion speeds up and access narrows. Novo's $675 list price from Jan 2027 [14], Foundayo self-pay at $149 [28] and the end of CVS medical exceptions [25] cut revenue per script; about 1 in 10 covering employers drop obesity coverage in 2027 [38, 39]; the market starts pricing the post-2027 Medicare cliff [42]; an NDA ruling at the 7th Circuit cuts retatrutide exclusivity to 5 years [43]. CY28 EPS estimates fall toward $46 and the stock trades at about 18x NTM EPS of about $46.

base.story: Volume beats price. CVS co-preferred status and Medicare (70% Lilly share of new seniors) keep tirzepatide on top [22, 25], Foundayo grows toward roughly $1.8B in 2027 [6], and the retatrutide BLA is filed in Q1 2027. CY27 EPS lands at about $47-49 and CY28 consensus drifts to about $53, so at the horizon the stock trades at about 23x NTM EPS of about $52.

bull.story: Foundayo compounds through telehealth and LillyDirect [27] and international launches, ACHIEVE-4's mortality signal helps uptake in type 2 diabetes [20], the 7th Circuit rules retatrutide a biologic (12-year exclusivity) [43], CMS signals a successor to the Bridge, and CY27/CY28 EPS beat to about $51/$57. The stock re-rates to about 27x on about $55.5 NTM EPS, near the top Street target ($1,600, Citi [33]).

thesis_break_reason: Below about $840 (27% under spot, about 17.7x CY27 consensus and below the lowest Street target of about $930 [33]), together with 2027/2028 EPS estimates being cut toward about $42/$45, the price would be signalling a fundamental break rather than ordinary volatility. LLY has had 23-34% drawdowns without broken fundamentals, so the level alone is not enough. Possible causes: tirzepatide net price falling well beyond the -9% underlying of Q2 after the Jan 2027 resets [1, 14], employer coverage losses running well above the roughly 10% surveys expect [38, 39], no Medicare successor to the Bridge [42], an NDA ruling plus a retatrutide safety issue [43], or a clear share loss to oral or next-gen rivals [3, 6]. Unchanged at $840; I keep it because my fair value moved only about 3%.

key_uncertainties: How fast US net price per script falls. Q2 US price was -3% reported but about -9% excluding rebate true-ups, and worldwide was -13%. CVS co-preferred status and $149 Foundayo self-pay add volume at lower price.
Employer coverage: about 67% of large employers cover obesity GLP-1s (BGH; Mercer says 44%), and roughly 1 in 10 of them expect to drop it in 2027.
The Medicare Bridge ends 2027-12-31 with no successor, which becomes a 2028 volume and multiple overhang by the horizon.
Whether Foundayo keeps gaining on the Wegovy pill (about 47.5k vs about 137-172k weekly IQVIA scripts). IQVIA undercounts the cash and telehealth channels.
The 7th Circuit ruling on retatrutide classification (12 vs 5 years of exclusivity) and the retatrutide FDA review timing (approval inside the horizon is not the base case).
Competition from Novo: the 2027 list-price cut, the CagriSema FDA decision (likely December 2026).
Product-liability MDLs: 3,848 gastroparesis cases with a Rule 702 ruling pending, and about 110 NAION cases in MDL 3163.
reasoning: Round 2. I took the supervisor's findings as corrections. (1) The material one: my 2028 EPS of $56.5 (2027 x 1.19) was 7-10% above published consensus of $51-53 (MarketScreener $51.01 [40], ChartMill $52.69 [41], 24/7 Wall St $52.29), whose revenue path is only about +11.6%. I re-based to $53.5, about $1 above the top of the consensus range, because 2027 estimates have been revised up faster than the 2028 aggregates and the Foundayo upgrade and CVS access are recent; NTM EPS falls from $54.0 to $52.0. (2) Medicare: the Bridge ends 2027-12-31 with BALANCE Part D delayed indefinitely [42]; I had not modelled that cliff, so I trimmed the CY27 multiple from 25.5x to 25.0x. (3) The retatrutide BLA/NDA appeal was argued at the 7th Circuit on Sep 24 and is under advisement [43, 44]; I added it as a dated two-way catalyst and a branch in the bear and bull cases. (4) CagriSema most likely lands in December, out of the 1-month window. (5) September was flat [45], so no rebound tilt. Acting on the source review, I dropped the low-signal alt-data (job listings [16], Google Trends [17], the Pew note [19]) from any role in the numbers, and used my follow-up searches (7) for alternative data that can move a number. Employer surveys: BGH finds 67% of large employers cover obesity GLP-1s and about 1 in 10 of those expect to drop it in 2027, and Mercer finds 5% of 500+ employers plan to drop it (44% coverage) [38, 39, 46]. That supports holding 2028 EPS near consensus rather than above it. I looked for weekly IQVIA Zepbound data after the CVS switch and for LillyDirect/telehealth channel share but found nothing published yet; that stays a watch item. Valuation: blended P/E fair value of $1,175 (from $1,215). I disagree slightly with the supervisor's $1,160: I keep 2028 EPS a little above consensus for the revision lag, so mine lands about 1% higher. Scenarios: $830 / $1,190 / $1,500 at 25/50/25, a mean of about $1,178. Ladder: a lognormal with median $1,165 (from $1,205) and an 80/20 mixture of 30% and 42% sigma (from 31%/45%). That thins the right tail (P(>=2300) from 0.030 to 0.020, P(>=2875) from 0.007 to 0.004), as the supervisor asked, since a consensus path with 2028 growth of about 12% does not support a fat upper tail. 30% is a little under the 35% realized vol because last year included one-off trial and policy shocks. P(>= spot) is 0.516.
